What the survey established

THE SHARPEST ATTACK ON THE DIRECTION IS DEFUSED, BY CONSTRUCTION. The winning shape (Tier 2: at viewport 1024 the list pane yields and the inspector docks in flow) was argued to collide head-on with the epic's one genuinely non-vacuous wide lock — display_state/4's 40-cell exhaustive table of hardcoded literals, and D94(a)'s clause that the wide/standard table is unchanged, pinned by literal constants. The display-state-seam survey settles the mechanics: collapse?/3 and display_state/4 are pure functions dispatched by Elixir arity and pattern; an inspector-aware display_state/5 never touches the /4 clauses, so the /4 table is not edited at all. No test anywhere in api/test/barkpark_web/studio or the live/studio directory asserts on arity, __info__, function_exported? or an export list. There is exactly ONE production call site in the whole tree — components.ex's studio_live_shell/1 pane-row loop — so the blast radius of a fifth argument is one line, using the Map.get(assigns, …, default) idiom already present there. The docs/cards/studio.md anchor is a substring match and is unaffected by a new arity. D94(a) is satisfied by construction rather than by argument.

THE FIFTH INPUT ALREADY EXISTS AS SERVER STATE, AND IS NOT WIRED. sidebar_user_opened (charter D91) seeds false in Shared.Paper.sidebar_assigns/1 and is raised only by Handlers.Paper.sidebar_toggle_panel/1 — which is a PURE ASSIGN FLIP. It does not call Shared.rebuild_panes/1, does not touch panes, does not touch width_bucket. Today it is threaded only to the inspector aside as data-user-opened. Consequence, and this is the mechanical statement of the direction's claim that step one of the ladder was skipped: on a sidebar toggle, display_state/4's inputs are unchanged, so its output for every pane cell is byte-identical, LiveView sends no patch to the pane row, and the rail does not move. The overlay and scrim below wide are implemented ENTIRELY in CSS via an @container panel query reacting to [data-width-bucket] and [data-user-opened]. Tier 2 therefore costs real plumbing in three places — an event that triggers a pane-visibility recompute, a fifth input on the ladder, and a reconciliation so the CSS overlay grammar and the Elixir ladder make ONE decision instead of two independent ones. Bounded and localised to pane_builder.ex, handlers/paper.ex, components.ex and root.html.heex, all inside the barkpark_web fence — but not a one-line change.

THE ARITHMETIC SPLITS CLEANLY INTO A PROVEN HALF AND AN UNPROVEN HALF. The identity rails + panel_px == viewport_px holds in ALL 54 rows of the committed table, zero exceptions, at every width, state and face; surface_max_width_px is 720 in all 54; content_px equals surface_border_box_px minus gutter total in all 54. So the first step of the Tier-2 chain — rail [44, 260] to [44], panel 720 to 980 at viewport 1024 — follows from a measured identity and needs no new assumption. The SECOND half does not. No row in the committed table has the inspector in a docked, in-flow, non-absolute position at ANY width; inspector.position is absolute in every sub-wide row. The chain surface 980 minus 300 = 680, then min(680, 720) = 680, then content 600, then 60.00ch resolved Iowan at 10.0000 px/ch assumes the docked panel is subtracted from panel_px exactly the way the list rail currently is. That subtraction model is architecturally reasonable and is NOT a measured fact. It is the wave's headline prediction and must be registered BEFORE any run, per the standing law.

THERE ARE THREE BOX-ACCOUNTING MECHANISMS, NOT TWO, AND A BUILDER CAN CONFLATE THEM. (i) Today's user-opened overlay: position absolute, overlap 260px over the content box, scrim covering the content box fully at alpha 0.55. (ii) The b29 default state below wide: an in-flow strip whose width is INTRINSIC (the head's 8px/12px padding plus the collapse icon), not a literal — at 1024 it shows surface_border_box_px 679 against panel_px 720, a 41px cost. (iii) The proposed Tier-2 dock, which exists nowhere yet. Any slice brief that treats (ii) and (iii) as the same kind of number will underestimate its own diff: (ii) is padding-and-icon rework, (iii) is new geometry.

TIER 1 IS FREE, AND SO IS THE b29 RULE. The overlay and scrim block is scoped inside @container panel (max-width: 860px); the b29/D91 painted-closed rule and its scrim guard are both scoped to html not-wide AND to :not([data-user-opened]). Net: neither b29 rule fires for the user-opened case this wave is about, so a user-opened shape must land as a NEW selector rather than a modification of them — and the wide bucket is already excluded from every rule in the family. Tier 1 should need zero CSS edits, which is a testable claim, not a hope.

D16 IS A REAL COLLISION THIS WAVE, NOT A HYPOTHETICAL. All five inspector-relevant selector families live in ONE contiguous span of root.html.heex at origin/main — the Responsive desk (spd-s1) section. Tier 2's rail-collapse CSS and Tier 3's destination-plus-scrim-suppression CSS both want the same sub-span. Two tiers cannot dispatch in the same round. spd-b12's dismissal work lives in components.ex and does NOT compete for that ownership, but is coupled to whatever the scrim rule becomes.

THE DISMISSAL SPINE HAS A REAL DESIGN FORK AND ONE CRITERION WITH ZERO PRECEDENT. The scrim is confirmed to be a bare ::after pseudo-element with pointer-events: none, and the stylesheet's own comment names spd-b12 as the owner of tap-to-dismiss in the .ex half — it structurally cannot carry a handler. spd-b12's criterion 1 cites two modals in components.ex (close-unpublish-guard, valueref-writeback-close) whose shape is a SEPARATE backdrop div carrying its own phx-click. But the repo's most recent and most relevant precedent is the secondary-picker fix (a8fb69cf7, D96): the backdrop DROPPED phx-click and dismissal moved to phx-click-away on the dialog card itself, because an inline onclick stopPropagation had killed every phx-click inside the card. D96 now forbids re-adding either. The inspector has no backdrop div at all. So criterion 1's literal precedent and the repo's hardened precedent point at different shapes — a fork Decide must rule, not a builder. Separately, criterion 3 (focus into the panel on open, return to the toggle on close, covered content inert or aria-hidden) has ZERO reusable precedent: no focus trap, no focus restore, no inert-marking helper exists anywhere in api/lib/barkpark_web or api/assets, and none of the roughly twenty inline hooks does it. That is new engineering. And criterion 4 needs an Elixir-visible 'am I in the overlay tier' signal, which today exists ONLY as a CSS container query with no server or JS mirror.

THE INSTRUMENT FAILS LOUD, NOT SILENT — AND THAT IS ITS OWN PROBLEM. If .bp-paper-surface is absent, two independent layers die(): sweepRow's REQUIRED_SELECTORS loop before any measurement, and PAGE_MEASURE's own fatal branch. It is never a silent zero. But the whole sweep is one try/finally with no per-row recovery, so a single die() discards the entire matrix including rows already collected. A Tier-3 destination state that legitimately has no reading column would, added naively, kill Tier 1 and Tier 2's rows in the same run. The third state needs four things that do not exist: a third navigation block, a state-conditional REQUIRED_SELECTORS (a real per-state required list, not a skip — the file's own doctrine forbids reporting a number derived from an element that is not there), a reading_column_present false / null-not-zero convention so nobody misreads 0 as catastrophic occlusion, and a fourth round-trip pass. Round-trip has nothing to call: no dismiss path is exercised anywhere in the instrument today, and spd-b12 is 0 of 4. The wish's own priority order already sequences the instrument AFTER the UI it measures; the survey confirms that ordering is forced, not preferred.

THE DEPLOY-AND-MEASURE LOOP IS FULLY MAPPED AND CHEAPER THAN FEARED. Changes under api/ on main auto-trigger deploy.yml; instance-deploy.sh clean-builds the idle slot, health-gates /api/schemas, flips the Caddy upstream. The instrument ssh-queries git rev-parse HEAD and the slot units once before the browser launches and once after the sweep closes, and a SHA or slot move between the two reads discards the whole matrix. Observed sweep runtimes are 29.8s, 30.9s, 32.8s and 59.7s — the '~10 minute run' is already corrected in the committed script and cited to D115; the risk is only that someone quotes the old number from memory. The zero-byte failure was an asymmetric realpath comparison in the entrypoint guard and is fixed. The [data-user-opened] real-click marker fails roughly 1 in 3 and dies BEFORE writeRunArtifact, so nothing is written and retrying is safe. One trap worth stating loudly: guerrilla is 157.180.90.121, not the 89.167.28.206 in the repo CLAUDE.md prod micro-block — a builder following the router literally will ssh to the wrong host and read an irrelevant SHA.

THE GATE ROSTER IS KNOWN AND ONE CARD IS AT ITS CAP. A root.html.heex plus .ex PR trips the ONE doc-gates job (25 named steps, confirmed by count) plus the Elixir workflow (mix-test and mix-prod-compile blocking, format advisory). root.html.heex is itself a design/emit.mjs ARTIFACT, but its single BEGIN/END GENERATED tokens marker pair sits far above the inspector region, so no tier risks the silent-deletion trap in this section. Where the survey CONTRADICTS the direction (all of it must be reconciled before Decide)

1. THE MD3 CITATION IS OVERSTATED, AND TWO INDEPENDENT SURVEYORS CAUGHT IT. The wish states MD3 puts 1024-1440px in a dockable-over-modal tier. D129 already corrected D101 on exactly this: the accurate citation is a two-tier standard/modal taxonomy at 600-1199dp in which standard sheets SHRINK rather than overlay, and MD3 only endorses a third pane or dock at 1600dp and above — ABOVE every width this wave tests. Viewport 1024 falls inside 600-1199dp and the shrink-not-overlay principle genuinely supports Tier 2; the three-pane docked configuration at 1024-1440 is NOT MD3-endorsed. Repeating the wish phrasing in a charter D-entry would re-commit the exact over-claim D129 had to strike, in the wave that inherits D129.

2. SANITY IS WIDTH-UNCONFIRMED AND ITS MECHANISM IS RICHER THAN "DRILL". D129 retains the behaviour but marks the triggering widths unconfirmed. The sourced mechanism is panes collapsing into a TAB BAR plus drill. Calling Tier 3 "Sanity's shape" must stay hedged as directional support, and if Tier 3 ships a bare full-screen destination with no tab-bar element, that divergence from the sourced comparable should be deliberate and stated, not silent.

3. TIER 3's "THE BREADCRUMB DRILL THAT ALREADY SHIPS CARRIES THE READER BACK" IS ASPIRATIONAL, NOT SHIPPED. desk_crumbs renders only at the phone bucket, and every clickable crumb is a PANE INDEX firing expand-pane with phx-value-idx; the handler truncates nav_path and push_patches a URL built from pane segments alone. The editor's own crumb is unconditionally static text with aria-current, never a button — a dead end, not a link. The editor closes as a SIDE EFFECT of the pane path shrinking, because handle_params re-derives editor_doc from the URL. At phone with an editor open, display_state returns :hidden for EVERY pane — no 44px strip survives, and crumbs are the only navigation surface left. There is no crumb kind for a non-pane destination. Making the inspector a summoned destination reachable by this drill needs either a new event and crumb kind or an extension of nav_path's model to make the editor an addressable node. The component's own doc comment guarantees "zero new server events" — a guarantee scoped to pane navigation only. Tier 3 is therefore larger than "extend a shipped pattern," and the direction's size framing for it must be corrected before slices are cut.

4. D102's RUNTIME RULE-DELETION DIFF IS NOT COMMITTED TOOLING. The direction requires any slice to prove wide moved zero pixels "by D102's runtime rule-deletion diff." A repo-wide search for deleteRule( returns zero hits; studio-desk-measure.mjs has no CSS-mutation capability, only the D97 provenance bracket. D102 was an ad hoc session whose RESULT was recorded in charter prose and whose TOOL did not survive. Commit df30ad4b2 (spd-w5) added the reading column's own container-name/container-type declaration as a fifteenth entry, and that entry deliberately DOES apply at 1280 and 1440 — it declares no box geometry, only which box a query resolves against, so it does not violate the wide-moves-zero-pixels property. Any brief quoting 14 will send a builder to "fix" a discrepancy that is not one.

The builder named the asymmetry in his own review and asked a reviewer to push on it; Review did. `openInspectorByRealClick` gains `fatal` (default true, so the matrix sweep and `user_opened_proof` keep D97 semantics — an unreached user-opened row is not a desk fact) and the round trip passes `fatal: false`, returning a named skip symmetric with `dismissInspectorByRealClick`, which already skipped rather than threw.
A filed backlog item whose premise Review disproved

`summoned-destination-position-coupling-untested` was filed by slice 2's builder against himself, claiming the lock "pins the four properties INDEPENDENTLY, so it would stay green on three of four" if `position: absolute` were dropped. Review settled it by mutation rather than by reading: stripping `position: absolute` from the narrow/phone rule REDS the suite, 11 tests / 1 failure, failing by name — "the summoned-destination rule no longer declares `position` — its geometry is gone". So the silent-revert hazard cannot occur silently, and the task's criterion 1 is already satisfied by the shipped test. The task was corrected on the ledger (dated reviewer note, priority dropped to 4) rather than left to send a future builder chasing a non-issue. What genuinely survives is only the narrower implication-form hardening. This is worth naming as a POSITIVE: the builder's instinct to file against himself was right even though this particular fear was not — the epic wants that instinct, and the correction costs one measurement.
Ledger audit

HONEST — no lies to fix on the wave's own four tasks. All four left `lifecycle: in_progress`, stamped every non-merge criterion with substantial evidence as they worked (361–1820 bytes per criterion, concrete and run-derived), and correctly left the merge-gated criterion `met: false` with EMPTY evidence for the lead to close on merge. All four parent to `spd-b39-user-opened-inspector-shape-successor`. Three discovered-but-not-taken items were filed AND published during the run (`spd-b47-ladder-backstrip-expand-collision`, `summoned-destination-position-coupling-untested`, `desk-measure-printer-proof-harness`). The three deferred slices (`wide-geometry-lock-sees-the-inspector`, `inspector-dismissal-and-return-grammar`, `inspector-shape-bracketed-deployed-run`) sit `open` and UNCLAIMED, exactly as the sequenced-rounds law requires — their absence from this wave is design, not failure. Review's own ledger writes: the position-coupling correction above, and one new published child, `charter-citation-resolves-guard`.
What the lead must know before merging

(1) MERGE ORDER IS NOT FREE. Slice 2 makes the exit MORE load-bearing than before: the panel now covers the content pane completely, so the only way out is the single `.bp-doc-sidebar__collapse` button — verified present and a real `<button>` with `aria-expanded`, so it is not a dead end — with no Escape, no focus trap, no focus return and no `aria-modal`. `inspector-dismissal-and-return-grammar` owns exactly that and is ROUND 2. Shipping Tier 3 before it is an honest, bounded regression in escapability, and the lead should decide deliberately rather than discover it. (2) `spd-b47` IS INHERITED, NOT NEW: the ladder's surviving 44px back-strip reuses the `narrow`-with-editor rule VERBATIM, so its `expand-pane` behaviour at `standard` is identical to what already ships at `narrow` today. Worth settling; the ladder did not create it. (3) NOTHING IN THIS WAVE HAS RUN IN A BROWSER against the deployed build. Every ch figure is transcribed from the committed 54-row table, never re-derived and never cross-face divided. The round trip, the destination state, the positive control and `PAGE_MEASURE_CHROME` are code that has never printed. (4) MERGE-GATED CRITERIA THE LEAD CLOSES: slice 1 index 6, slice 2 index 5, slice 3 index 6, slice 4 index 7 — one "PR merged" criterion each, all four correctly left unstamped.
Grade — A−

WHAT EARNS IT. The wave answered D127's handed-over question in geometry that exists in the tree, not in prose: a ladder keyed to how much room there actually is, with each tier's refusal reasoned rather than asserted. The half-suspended read D127 ruled a DEFECT — prose at 55% black while the layout metric rises and the human loses 219px — does not survive at any width in any state after this wave. Three of four slices were mutation-proven by their own builders BEFORE Review, and every one of those proofs reproduced when Review re-ran it. The additive-arity design is genuinely elegant: it buys a fifth input without costing the existing 40-cell lock a single byte, and the equivalence bridge is what keeps that from being a technicality. The builders were unusually honest — two filed tasks against their own work, one refused a brief instruction that was factually wrong (the "invert four absent-assign tests" instruction, where the tests did not exist) and stamped the deviation rather than quietly dropping it, and slice 4's builder named the exact bug Review then fixed. D102's evaporated-harness provenance is closed with committed, re-runnable tooling whose ch-refusal guard fired on its own author's run-record key.

WHAT HOLDS IT BACK, and it is not the deferred rounds. The charter defect is a wave-level failure, not a slice-level one: the Paper asserted a write it had not made, three slices shipped citations into a tree where they resolved to nothing, and Review had to repair the same class of defect for the second consecutive wave. The epic has now spent three waves learning one lesson. Second, slice 4 — the largest diff in the wave at 1126 insertions — has a gate of `node --check` plus `--help`, which is close to no gate at all, and its builder said plainly that nothing in it has run in a browser; the one bug Review found lived exactly in that unexercised region, which is evidence the gate is too thin rather than reassurance that review caught it. Third, the DELIVERABLE the wish names — measure the shipped shape against the DEPLOYED build with the prediction registered first — is genuinely not done this wave; that is legitimately round 3's and correctly sequenced, but it means the wave ships a shape whose central claims are still source-facts. Not an A, because a wave that repairs its own citation discipline at Review has not yet internalised it; comfortably above B+, because everything it actually built is correct, well-locked, honestly reported, and moves the wish forward.
What the next wave takes

MERGE ROUND 1 FIRST — all four slices are file-disjoint (`pane_builder.ex`/`components.ex`/`mount.ex`; `root.html.heex`; two new `scripts/` files; `studio-desk-measure.mjs`) and the charter amendment rides slice 1. Then dispatch by dependency, not by convenience. `wide-geometry-lock-sees-the-inspector` the MOMENT slice 2 merges — its census must enumerate the FINAL rule set, and today the lock passes 16 of 16 on a sheet mutated 300px → 200px while that same edit moves 1280 wide content 596px → 640px. `inspector-dismissal-and-return-grammar` once slices 1 AND 2 merge — it is the escapability debt this wave took on deliberately, and D154 fixes its shape (sibling scrim, `phx-click-away` REFUSED, the tier gate computed from `display_state/5`'s own inputs and never from `width_bucket`, since after the ladder 1024 is standard AND docked). Then, after all five merge and DEPLOY, `inspector-shape-bracketed-deployed-run` — the only artefact permitted to speak about the deployed render. Register D150's per-face prediction BEFORE the run so it can fail; forced Georgia's 54.31ch MISS at 1024 is EXPECTED and inherited (`spd-b42`), not overlay-caused. D153's positive control is MANDATORY, because a successful fix makes the non-vacuity guard vacuous and a drifted selector produces the identical zero. A zero-byte run is an INSTRUMENT FAILURE, never a desk fact.

tags.rationale: The whole wave is the Studio desk's user-summoned inspector and the reading measure it takes.
The central call is whether a summoned panel is a mode with the reading bar suspended, or must become something else entirely.
Every claim rides the committed 54-row instrument artifact and a deployed bracketed re-run.
The direction is a three-tier width ladder: wide docks, standard yields the list, narrow and below become a destination.
The mode claim is void without Escape, focus trap and restore, aria-modal and a truthful aria-expanded.
This is the wave's living strategy Paper, opened at Strategize and closed at Review.

documents.title: The inspector stops borrowing the reader's column — the desk pays for it in priority order

blocks.text: PD BLOCK WISHLIST · WAVE 1 · 2026-07-17

One hundred NEW block candidates for PortableDoc — deduped against the 62 canonical types (plus the TUI dashboard and this wave's blockquote), graded honestly per surface, priced by cost tier, and wired to real demand evidence. The companion Review paper ranks them by usefulness; this paper is the raw material, and it is written IN the product it describes.

content.value: Baseline: tiers.ex's 62 canonical types (25 element + 35 widget + 2 section, test-enforced) + TUI-only dashboard + blockquote (born this wave) — charter D1. Struck by the binding dedup verdicts (D9): linear gauge (stat max-bar + 1-row gauge-list cover it), toned callout (5 tones shipped), and generic "mermaid support" (the browser is a full pass-through). The chat-approval / chat-question / chat-plan rows once wished for are ALREADY first-class blocks — demand satisfied before this list was written.

Each entry: anchor + kebab type name, one-line pitch with its demand evidence, an Attrs-contract data-shape sketch (the ratified pbp-tui-creative-slate style), then one grade line: family · tier · cost · View · Edit (E0-E4) · TUI · React · Email. Grades are per surface and never inferred from each other (D2 — the React/Edit missing-sets overlap on only 4 of 14 items).

Data-viz Edit defaults to E3 — a JSON textarea is not WYSIWYG (D3). Email badges split REAL renders from degrades (D4). Cost tiers are calibrated on shipped datapoints (D6/D7): STATIC ~9-14 files; I1 dual hydration cost asciicast 30-40 files; I2 adds a route + security surface; in-canvas editability is a separate ~514-line STUDIO-EDIT surcharge. Blocks needing non-task data carry a resolver flag; plugin-domain blocks carry a seam flag (D10).

backend-write: I1 + new API route + resolver + security surface
in-canvas editability surcharge, ~514 lines / 8 files per block — separate from birth

content.value: Wave 4: install the teeth, and make the merge verb an artifact

Living wave Paper for WAVE 4 of the Honest Gates epic (root task auth-totp-tests-are-time-boundary-flaky, priority 0). Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-honest-gates-charter.md on origin/main @ f38c01920 — 246 lines, D1-D49. Predecessor Papers: gates-tell-the-truth-wave-2026-07-20 (wave 1), honest-gates-wave-2026-07-27 (wave 2), honest-gates-wave-2026-07-28 (wave 3). Every later phase appends HERE — Digest adds the survey digest and the verify plan before the verifiers fly; Decide adds the decisions and the slice roster before the builders fly; Review closes it as the debrief.
STATUS: Strategize complete — the wave is SURVEYING. The direction below is committed in shape and tentative in its details; two exploration rounds (survey, then verify) precede Decide.
The wish

Run wave 4 and close hgw2-s7-enable-branch-protection. Three consecutive waves have deferred it, each with a better reason than the last, and every one of those reasons is now paid off. The plain sentence that has survived every wave must not survive this one: nothing in this repo is required-by-name, and every ratchet waves 1-3 built is ADVISORY.

DONE MEANS: branches/main/protection returns 200 with enforce_admins.enabled true and the required contexts pinned; a throwaway PR with a RED required check has gh pr merge --admin REFUSED and the refusal quoted; the same PR merges once green; the fleet has a documented, working merge verb that is not --admin; and a break-glass exists that is one attributable command down, one back, and impossible to leave open silently.
Also in scope: close hgw2-s5-ci-verdict-reader honestly (PR #6414 is green and the lead will merge it), and DECIDE the claim-lease false red rather than documenting it again.
Ground truth, re-derived at Strategize (2026-07-28, origin/main @ f38c01920)
Every row below was measured in this phase against live GitHub or the live ledger. Nothing here is inherited on trust.
Claim
Measured
What it changes
Protection state
branches/main/protection = 404 Branch not protected; rulesets = []
D13 still stands verbatim. The wave's whole reason.
Repo merge flags
allow_auto_merge false, allow_squash_merge true, delete_branch_on_merge false, user-owned public repo
Auto-merge is a repo-setting change, not a per-PR one. User-owned kills merge queue AND may kill the audit log the break-glass wants.
PROCESS RULE 2 citation
bp-loop-ledger.md line 43 reads verbatim: 'This repo does NOT allow gh auto-merge — poll checks + gh pr merge --squash --admin'
The cited authority EXISTS and COVERS what it is cited for. Premise smoke: PASS.
Committed spec
.github/required-checks.json on main: enforced false, two checks pinned to app_id 15368 — 'Elixir gate' and 'PR references an active task', with 10 reasoned exclusions
The apply tooling and the spec exist. This wave regenerates and flips, it does not rebuild.
Fleet freeze, re-derived
15 open PRs. 4 render 'Elixir gate' (#6631 #6551 #6498 #6414). 11 render ZERO. All 15 render 'PR references an active task'.
The unfreeze is 11 PRs, not 12, and the two names have RADICALLY different freeze costs.
Skip-shim throughput, live
PR #6414: 'Elixir gate' concluded success in 2 SECONDS; four Elixir jobs 'skipping'
Requiring Elixir gate is ~13m39s only on api-touching PRs. On everything else it is seconds. This materially weakens the auto-merge necessity argument.
Main's own health
'Elixir gate' = success on the last three main shas whose runs actually completed (b43f5d7f, c8897f81, ad3b6d56). Format advisory = failure on all three.
The required name is main-green today. Format stays out (D10).
Main's queue collapse
11 of the last 12 main pushes have NO 'Elixir gate' conclusion at all — elixir runs at 11:40-11:42Z are 'cancelled' by queue collapse (D28 SUPERSEDED shape)
Criterion 10's 'main-green' must be read on shas whose run COMPLETED, or it reads a false red. Protection is unaffected: it evaluates PR heads.
Sobelow
security.yml runs green on main pushes (27352d8c, c0d27a0d) after the Felix inline-annotation migration
Irrelevant to protection either way — security.yml is paths-filtered and structurally disqualified. Any plan treating Sobelow greenness as a precondition is wrong.
Legacy Vercel poison
commits/f38c01920/status = failure; 'Vercel – demo' and 'Vercel – barkpark' (EN DASH) failure on every sha
The spec correctly uses checks with app_id, never contexts. A required set containing either is an instant deadlock.
The lapse grace is ALREADY exceeded, live
hgw2-s5-ci-verdict-reader: lifecycle open, claim.previous_worker lead-w3-land, claim.expired_at 2026-07-28T05:08:01Z — about 6h37m ago against a 21600s (6h) grace
The task gate would RED #6414 on its next fire. Requiring it today knowingly installs a false red. This is the lease decision, and it is not hypothetical.
The reap DOES stamp
hgw2-s5's claim carries previous_worker + expired_at + worker:null; hgw2-s2 carries released_at (the D23 ordering clause's real shape)
D23's predicate is REACHABLE. The hole is the grace WIDTH, not the mechanism.
Preconditions
hgw3-s7-charter-via-pr open 0/7; hgw2-s4-format-ceiling-reland open 0/12; hg-bl-enable-auto-merge-under-protection open 0/4 (a CHILD of s7); both D49 hotfix backlog items open
hgw3-s7 is a hard precondition (D39). The format ceiling is NOT — see the direction.
The direction: protection ships, and the merge protocol ships as an ARTIFACT, not a sentence

Wave 3 framed the blocker as 'protection needs a merge-protocol replacement.' That framing is right and incomplete. The replacement it proposed — rewrite PROCESS RULE 2 — is a SENTENCE, and this epic's own charter law says a slice is not done without part three: the population and the ratchet. A sentence has neither. D48 is the proof already in the record: the same merge folklore occurs 253 times across 68 files and its highest-leverage copy lives OUTSIDE the repo where no builder and no CI guard can reach it. A prose merge protocol is exactly the kind of predicate this epic exists to abolish — one that cannot be executed, cannot be tested, and cannot be proven able to fail.

So the centrepiece of this wave is not the PUT. The PUT is four minutes of work with tooling that already exists and is mutation-proven. The centrepiece is that THE FLEET'S MERGE VERB BECOMES A SINGLE EXECUTABLE ARTIFACT, and every prose site collapses into a pointer at it.

What the finished experience looks like. An agent finishes a slice, pushes, and runs one command — the sanctioned merge verb. It runs the deadlock detector FIRST (set difference of the committed spec against the check runs actually rendered on the head, exit 3 as a third state), so a PR that can never merge is refused in seconds with the missing context NAMED — something GitHub itself will never tell you at N=2, where the refusal reads '2 of 2 required status checks are expected.' and names nothing. If the PR is merely not-yet-green, the verb waits within a bounded budget and merges the moment it goes green; if the wait exceeds the budget it hands off to GitHub's own auto-merge and says so. If a required check is genuinely red, it refuses and quotes the refusal. If the ledger is down, it says the ledger is down and names the exit. The agent never types --admin, never types --auto, and never has to know which of GitHub's six refusal shapes it is looking at. Every one of those shapes maps to one row of an enumerated exit table, and every row has one command.

And the break-glass is not a curl. A curl cannot be attributed on a user-owned repo and cannot be prevented from being left open. The break-glass becomes a script that CANNOT OPEN WITHOUT WRITING A RECORD: it refuses without a reason and a task id, writes the record to the ledger first, then DELETEs enforce_admins — and while it is open, the required-checks verify guard reds in CI, so the repo itself screams until it is closed. One attributable command down, one back, impossible to leave open silently — the wish's words, satisfied mechanically rather than by discipline.
The choices I lean toward, tentatively:

BOTH names on day one, as the committed spec already pins: 'Elixir gate' + 'PR references an active task'. D43's refusal of a ratchet-free required set stands, and Elixir gate is where every ratchet waves 1-3 built actually rides.

hgw3-s7-charter-via-pr is a HARD precondition and ships in round 1. D39 is L1: protection rejects a direct push with GH006, and 12.7% of main arrives that way from the epic-cycle's own Decide phase. Without it, every concurrent wave hangs at Decide the day the flip lands.

hgw2-s4-format-ceiling-reland is NOT a precondition and must not gate the flip. It adds a blocking job to the aggregator's needs, which changes Elixir gate's COMPOSITION, not the required NAME. It carries its own hazard in the other direction (a stale roster reds the required context repo-wide), so it lands BEFORE the flip with a fresh roster or it is explicitly deferred with the hazard named — never squeezed in after.

The lease gets DECIDED, not documented, and it is a hard sibling of the flip rather than a nice-to-have. The 6h grace is already exceeded on a live PR's own task. Requiring the task gate on top of a predicate we have measured to be currently false is installing a known false red — the epic's disease inside the epic's own flip.

allow_auto_merge: lean YES, but as a MECHANISM the artifact invokes behind a mandatory pre-flight, never as a protocol agents type. The wave decides it on evidence (the api-PR ratio, real merge dwell) and adopts hg-bl-enable-auto-merge-under-protection rather than re-filing it (D14).
The fleet unfreeze is executed and evidenced, not asserted — with one measurement first that could collapse its cost by an order of magnitude (survey key unfreeze-cost).

What to prioritise if the wave has to choose. The flip beats everything, and the flip is cheap. The merge verb beats the format ceiling. The lease decision beats the format ceiling. The format ceiling is the thing to drop.
The direction debate: four rivals, argued

RIVAL 1 — FLIP AND FOLLOW. Install protection with the two names; the merge-protocol replacement is 'delete one flag' (D40 measured that a plain gh pr merge --squash merges under enforce_admins:true the moment the required context goes green); rewrite PROCESS RULE 2; decide auto-merge NO. Smallest possible change, lowest blast radius, ships in one round.

Why it loses. It is the wave-3 plan with the deferral removed, and it repeats a mistake the charter already documented. A prose-only merge verb has no population step and no ratchet, and D48 measured what happens to prose in this fleet: 253 occurrences, 68 files, and the one that reaches every session automatically lives in a different repository. Worse, it leaves each agent to interpret GitHub's refusal themselves — and D38 measured that at N=2 the refusal names NOTHING, and that a deadlock and a red are only distinguishable by a set difference nobody is doing. An agent that cannot tell a deadlock from a red, holding a token with admin rights, will open the glass. That is D13 a fifth time by a different door.

RIVAL 2 — THE MERGE VERB BECOMES AN ARTIFACT (the winner). Same flip; the deliverable is one executable merge verb plus one executable break-glass, both harnessed and mutation-proven, and every prose site — bp-loop-ledger.md:43, .claude/agents/felix.md:44, connectors/README.md:189, docs/ops/merge-gates.md, and the out-of-repo memory file as a lead action — repointed at them.

Why it wins. It is the only rival that satisfies the epic's own acceptance law. CAUSE: protection installed with enforce_admins true. POPULATION: every merge path in the fleet repointed, not the one sentence that happened to be cited. RATCHET: the verb's own harness, the break-glass that cannot open silently, the verify guard that reds while it is open, and a tripwire that reds if --admin reappears as a sanctioned verb. It also converts the auto-merge question from a fleet-wide behavioural change into an implementation detail behind a pre-flight — which is precisely how to absorb the sharpest objection against it.

RIVAL 3 — STAGE THE TEETH: protect with ONE name today, add the second once the fleet is unfrozen. Genuinely attractive: it kills the plain sentence within the hour and makes a fifth deferral structurally impossible, because protection would already be installed when the unfreeze work begins. The obvious staging is 'task gate first' — it renders on 15 of 15 open PRs, so the freeze cost is ZERO, it re-fires without a push (D43), and its p50/p90 are 16s/57s.

Why it loses, and why its INVERSE survives as a fallback. Task-gate-first is the worst possible single name: it is the ONE required context whose verdict depends on guerrilla, a host measured at 2.8-10.3s under concurrent waves that 500s outright on large payloads, and whose lapse predicate is measurably false RIGHT NOW on hgw2-s5. Requiring it alone means one ledger outage deadlocks the entire repository with no other check to reason from, and D49's only documented exit — the hotfix! label — needs a push to engage and records nothing. The INVERSE staging (Elixir gate only on day one, task gate second) is strictly safer: it depends on GitHub alone. It survives as the wave's fallback if the unfreeze or the lease decision proves more expensive than measured — but it is not the plan, because both names are already pinned in a spec that was generated, selection-tested across 8 heads of different path shapes, and reviewed.

RIVAL 4 — FIX THE LEASE AND THE HOTFIX BREAK-GLASS FIRST, FLIP NEXT WAVE. Honest-sounding: do not require a gate you have measured to be currently lying. Rejected as deferral #5 wearing a lab coat. The lease fix is a predicate change in one script with an existing 62-fixture harness; it is a SIBLING of the flip, not a prerequisite round. Sequencing it as a prerequisite is exactly the move that produced three better-reasoned deferrals.
The sharpest attack on the winner, and how the wave absorbs it

THE ATTACK. 'The merge verb as an artifact' introduces a new mandatory tool to a fleet of roughly 250 agent-runs a day that reads prose and acts on habit. D26 is the charter's own warning: a harness nobody runs is not a ratchet. If agents keep typing gh pr merge --squash --admin from muscle memory, the artifact changes nothing — except that now the habitual command FAILS LOUDLY, and the agent's most natural recovery, holding a token with repo admin, is to open the glass. The wave would then have built a beautifully-harnessed verb nobody uses and a break-glass everybody does. That is D13 a fifth time, installed by the wave that was supposed to end it.
HOW THE WAVE ABSORBS IT. Four ways, and they are acceptance criteria, not intentions.

GRACEFUL DEGRADATION. The verb is a THIN wrapper. If an agent ignores it entirely and runs a plain gh pr merge --squash, that still works and still respects protection — D40 measured it. The artifact adds pre-flight and waiting; it does not add a required dependency. Only --admin breaks, and only when it should.

THE POPULATION LANDS IN THE SAME SESSION AS THE FLIP. Not the same wave — the same session. The three live agent-facing prose sites plus merge-gates.md ship in the flip's own PR, and the out-of-repo memory file is a named LEAD ACTION executed alongside, because no builder worktree can reach it (D48).

THE GLASS IS DELIBERATELY HIGHER-FRICTION THAN THE CORRECT PATH. Merging correctly is one command with no arguments. Opening the glass demands a reason and a task id, writes a record before it acts, and makes CI red until it is closed. The friction gradient must point at the correct path, and that is testable.

ADOPTION IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. 'The same PR merges once green' generalises: the wave does not close until real fleet merges have gone through the new verb and the audit of what actually happened is in the debrief. If the fleet routes around the verb, that is a finding this wave must report, not one the next wave discovers.

A second, quieter attack worth naming: requiring 'PR references an active task' makes LEDGER HYGIENE a merge blocker on a host that degrades. The wave's answer is that this is a real cost accepted with eyes open, bounded by the lease decision and by an enumerated outage exit — and that the fallback staging (Elixir gate only) exists precisely for the case where survey shows guerrilla's availability cannot support it.

7. What the survey SETTLED, so no builder re-derives it

Guerrilla is not the risk. 1550 unauthenticated reads across six load levels: zero timeouts, zero 200-with-null, worst latency 1.56s against a 20s cap. Rate limiting starts between -P 10 and -P 25 from ONE IP; the gate makes one GET per PR event from IP-diverse runners. No retry to tune, no caching layer, no fallback host.

The gate is honest in five of six degraded shapes: connection-refused, 503, 429 and a 200 with garbage all exit 2 UNCHECKED after bounded retry. Never a silent green. The SIXTH — 200 with a well-formed null result — takes the `missing` branch and DEFINITIVELY accuses a correct PR. And that branch is reachable ONLY via 200-with-null, because a nonexistent id AND a real-id/wrong-type read both return 404 handled elsewhere. So rerouting it to UNCHECKED loses no true detection whatsoever.

No security.yml check can ever be required — confirmed independently from the spec's own exclusion list, which names both security.yml contexts as S4 PATHS-FILTERED. Sobelow's greenness is NOT a precondition for protection. doc-gates.yml and go-tests.yml are likewise structurally disqualified.

The main-green reading has an honest rule. Queue collapse on main is DOCUMENTED, INTENDED behaviour (cancel-in-progress is explicitly false on main; the comment says 'Queued main runs collapse to one'), and it is main-ref-scoped: PR-ref elixir runs are 0 cancelled / 15 success / 1 real failure. Read the newest main push whose elixir run reached a terminal non-cancelled conclusion. Today that is 27352d8c1 and it is GREEN — while the naive tip read of f38c01920 returns no such check run and would be mis-narrated as a false red.

THE D49 CREATE REGRESSION HAS NOT CLEARED, and wave 3's wave-log note saying it had is wrong. bp task create, bp doc create task and raw /v1/data/mutate creates alternated between 'unknown error', HTTP 500 and client timeouts across FOURTEEN reviewer attempts spanning about six minutes, while reads, patches, publishes, claims, stamps and pulses stayed healthy throughout — the same asymmetry two builders reported hours earlier. One task landed early in the window (hgw4-bl-merge-verb-names-the-run-id, filed and published for the S2 builder whose six attempts had failed); one did not. This is not a nuisance: 'PR references an active task' is about to become required against this same host, so an outage that blocks task CREATION becomes an outage that blocks a fleet from opening PRs.

THE ITEM THAT ALMOST DID NOT MAKE IT ONTO THE BOARD — it is filed now, and the fight to file it is itself the finding. hgw4-bl-disable-bypasses-recording-glass is PUBLISHED, priority 1, parented under the epic, five acceptance criteria. It took roughly TWENTY create attempts across two windows, and the call that finally worked reported nothing: a later retry answered 'document already exists', which is how the reviewer learned the draft had landed. THE TRAP WORTH RECORDING FOR EVERY FUTURE PHASE: a bp create that REPORTS FAILURE may nevertheless have landed as a draft, so read the draft back (bp doc get task drafts.<id> --perspective raw) before re-filing, or you will conclude work is unfiled when it is merely unpublished. The body: scripts/required-checks-apply.sh --disable removes ALL branch protection after nothing but --confirm and records nothing, so the recording invariant is a MECHANISM for the narrow glass and only a CONVENTION for the total hammer; breakglass.sh --close only POSTs enforce_admins and cannot repair a --disable. Scoped honestly, because the builder overstated it: this is UNRECORDED, not SILENT — breakglass-watch.sh reads UNPROTECTED and reds with 'BREAK-GLASS OPEN (total)' when the committed spec says enforced=true, so the wish's 'impossible to leave open silently' is actually satisfied; what is missing is attribution. The fix is four steps, on the task. Fold it into hgw2-s7, which already touches that script.

A LIVE GAP THE FLIP MUST ANSWER, found by this wave's own charter PR. #6689 carries the wave-log entry and its 'PR references an active task' check is RED — correctly, by the gate's own rule. The only task it could honestly name is the epic parent auth-totp-tests-are-time-boundary-flaky, which is an open, unclaimed Goal. Under protection this PR could not merge, and both ways out are wrong: claiming a long-lived Goal misrepresents its lifecycle, and naming a sibling slice task is a lie. This is not hypothetical and it is not one PR's problem — hgw3-s7 (#6688) routes EVERY future epic-cycle charter through exactly this shape, so the day the task gate is required, every wave's own charter PR deadlocks. Round 2 must decide it: either the epic-cycle files a per-wave wave-log task, or the gate learns that a Goal-typed parent backs its own charter PR. The five slice PRs (#6684-#6688) are all green on both required contexts, so this is specific to the charter shape.
Cross-slice integration

All five -r branches merge onto current origin/main with ZERO conflicts, and every wave-4 gate is green in that one integrated tree: pr-task-gate 73/0, bp-merge 28/0, required-checks selftest 16/16, break-glass 55/0, doc budgets PASS, docs-anchors PASS, and module-scope smoke OK on all four workflow files. The slices are genuinely file-disjoint, which is why the frontier dispatched them in parallel and why they cohere: S2 and S3 both consume required-checks-verify.sh but only S2 edits it, and S3's gate runs S2's selftest against origin/main's copy, so the two agree in both directions.

The one coherence gap worth naming is not a conflict but an absence: nothing in the repo POINTS at scripts/bp-merge.sh yet. bp-loop-ledger.md PROCESS RULE 2 still says gh pr merge --squash --admin, and merge-gates.md, felix.md and connectors/README.md still carry the same folklore. That repointing is hgw2-s7's own criterion 16 and lands with the flip by design — but until it does, the fleet has a merge verb nobody has been told about.
Grade: B+

What earns it. Every slice did the hard version. S1 could have widened the grace to 24h and moved on; instead it DELETED the tunable and replaced a time-varying predicate with a fixed one, then wrote the cost of that narrowing into the code rather than into a changelog nobody reads. S2 could have been a bash alias; instead it is a seven-state refusal table keyed on the string because the exit code was measured to carry no information, with a pure classifier seam that lets the whole table be harnessed over captured fixtures with no token — and along the way it found that the deadlock detector was returning green on a permanently frozen head. S3 proved its ordering claim AT THE API CALL by snapshotting the log inside a gh stub, rather than asserting it from source, which is the difference between a proof and a description. S5 refused to reinstate either of the two broken gates it inherited and built a third. And four of five builders named holes in their own work in writing, unprompted, including the two the reviewer then had to close.

What holds it below an A. The wish's headline — INSTALL THE TEETH — did not happen, and while the sequencing is correct and defensible, a wave graded against this wish cannot call that a rounding error: protection is still 404 and the fourth consecutive wave ends with every ratchet advisory. Beyond that, two defects that reached the reviewer should not have. The invalid permissions scope shipped a workflow that GitHub would have refused to parse — a scream that never runs, in the slice whose entire subject is silence, and it is the SECOND wave in a row where a YAML defect walked past a green script harness. And the skipped conclusion shipped as an explicitly-labelled guess in a merge verb, where a wrong guess means refusing a mergeable head. Both were found by reading, not by any gate. There is also almost no live exercise anywhere in this wave: bp-merge's merge_loop and preflight have never touched a real protected PR, breakglass.sh has never run against the real repo, and the watch workflow has never executed — every proof here is hermetic, which is honest but is not the same as working.

One thing that is NOT held against the wave: the branches are pushed and the PRs are open. Six consecutive waves ended with reviewed, gate-passing work sitting on local-only branches in a shared checkout that other cycles reset. #6684 through #6689 exist.
What the next wave takes

ROUND 2, in dispatch order, the moment its dependencies merge. hgw2-s7-enable-branch-protection after S1 + S2 + S3 (#6684, #6685, #6686) — this is THE FLIP and everything it was waiting for is now on a branch. Two instructions the reviewer would add to its brief. First: run the throwaway-PR proof THROUGH scripts/bp-merge.sh rather than around it, because S7's proof is the only opportunity in sight to exercise the merge verb's live paths, and a wrapper whose merge_loop has never run under enforce_admins is a wrapper the fleet will discover is broken at the worst moment. Second: fold in hg-bl-disable-bypasses-recording-glass, whose body is above, since S7 already touches the apply script. Then hg-bl-hotfix-breakglass-records-nothing after S1 (#6684), which edits the same workflow file.

LEAD ACTIONS this wave could not do from a worktree: merge #6414 and close hgw2-s5-ci-verdict-reader's ninth criterion on its claim epoch (8 of 9 are stamped and waiting); dispatch the genuinely independent second review of S1's P4 predicate, which this workflow structurally cannot spawn; provision the BREAKGLASS_TOKEN secret, without which the scream's live authority is unarmed; file hg-bl-disable-bypasses-recording-glass if the ledger recovers before S7 runs; and update the out-of-repo ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md:31 push mandate, which still carries the pre-GH006 framing.

Wave 4 did not install the teeth. It built every tool the dentist refused to work without, proved each one able to fail, and put them on branches with the PRs open — including the one that would have gone in as a scream GitHub could not even parse. The plain sentence is still true: nothing in this repo is required-by-name. It is now false by three merges, and every one of them is a link you can click.
